name: thumb-notch
title: Thumb Notch
description: A long-list jump index die-cut into the scroll surface itself — staggered semicircular notches clipped from the right edge, one per group, descending diagonally like a hardback dictionary's thumb index, deeper and lighter for whichever group is on screen.
useWhen: a long alphabetical or grouped list (contacts, glossaries, log dates, country pickers) that needs a jump index carved into its own scroll edge — semicircular clip-path notches, deeper for the on-screen group, readable at rest with no scrollbar and no floating rail on top of the content. Pick listbox-sticky-groups instead when the list's own passed group HEADERS should be the navigation, stacking into a clickable trail as they scroll past — that component moves content to build its index; this one never moves anything, it cuts the index into the edge once and depth alone tells you where you are.
instruction: A grouped long-list jump index built from two adjacent panels sharing one seam: a scrollable content panel on the left and a fixed-width notch nav on the right, painted later in DOM order so its buttons sit on top of the seam with zero z-index management. MECHANISM: the content panel's own clip-path is a generated `path("M0,0 L w,0 L w,y0-r A r,r 0 0 0 w,y0+r L w,y1-r ... L w,h L0,h Z")` — one concave semicircular bite cut from its right edge per group, y-positions spread evenly down the panel's ResizeObserver-measured height, bite radius 7px for a resting group and 11px for whichever group is on screen. The nav renders one real `<button aria-label="Jump to {letter}">` per group, a filled circle (1px larger radius than its matching bite, 8px resting / 12px active) centered exactly on the shared seam via `left:0` + `translate(-50%,-50%)` — its background matches the panel's, so the letter appears to sit inside the die-cut without any layer depending on clip-path hit-testing for interaction: the button is always the real, always-focusable, always-clickable target: the clip-path is presentation only. The on-screen group is detected by comparing each group header's plain `.offsetTop` (relative to a position:relative content wrapper, captured once via refs — deliberately NOT getBoundingClientRect, which would read a mid-shear transformed position) against live scrollTop, rAF-throttled on the scroll listener. SCRUB: pointerdown on any notch calls `setPointerCapture`, so a press-drag along the edge keeps reporting to that same handler regardless of which notch or gap is physically under the finger — each pointermove maps clientY against the nav's own measured bounding rect to the nearest group index. A small loupe pill (position:fixed, aria-hidden, border-ns-accent — the only static-ish use of accent, and it only exists while a pointer is actually down) follows the raw pointer coordinates offset up-left, showing the previewed letter live; a separate visually-hidden aria-live="polite" region receives 'Jump to {letter}' but only fires on an actual index CHANGE, never once per pixel of drag. COMMIT (the shear): on pointerup, a plain click, Enter/Space on a notch, or a typed letter matching a group (see below), the content wrapper's transform+opacity ease out (translateY 10px, 150ms ease-in) as if the visible page is sliding away; 30ms later — while still faded — scrollTop is set directly to the target group's captured offsetTop, the wrapper is repositioned to the opposite 10px offset with transitions off, then eased back to identity on ease-out-expo (cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), ~320ms) — read as riffling the book open rather than a bare scrollTo. A 150ms de-dupe guard on the committed group id absorbs the native `click` that always follows a pointer tap or keyboard activation right after the pointerup/typeahead path already committed, so nothing double-plays. prefers-reduced-motion skips the whole sequence for a direct scrollTop write — depth and letter-color state (the resting 'you are here' read) are pure layout/color and are never gated on motion preference, only the shear itself is. A11Y: notches live inside a labelled `<nav aria-label="Alphabet index">`; every one is a real button with its own accessible name, so Tab always reaches something even with zero groups scrolled. The content panel is `role="region" tabIndex=0` with its own aria-label, and its onKeyDown implements the SAME native-<select>-style typeahead as a plain listbox (500ms buffer, matched against each group's letter, calling the identical commit function a notch tap uses) so keyboard users never need to touch a notch at all. Colors: resting notch depth/color is --foreground (active) vs --ns-muted (resting) only; --ns-accent appears solely on focus-visible rings and the drag-only loupe pill border, honoring the interaction-only rule. Cleans up its ResizeObserver, scroll rAF, shear timers/rAF, and typeahead timer on unmount. DEMO: a ~21-letter contact directory (skipping unused letters, like a real address book) in a 420px panel — real projects pass their own `groups`.
